questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is running a short safety drive on protecting the home. Write a notice for the school notice board in about 100 words. Give three precautions that students should take to keep valuables in the house safe, and name one thing about a house that makes it an easy target for a thief. Leave the date, the time and the name of the issuing club as blanks.

markingPoints.description: Format: a proper notice layout with the heading NOTICE, a title line, the advice set out in short lines, and the date, time and name of the issuing club left as blanks.

Content: gives three clear precautions for keeping valuables safe in the house, such as keeping jewellery and money in a bank rather than in a safe at home, never hanging the key to the house or kitchen door on a hook outside, and having a strong burglar alarm fitted.
Content: names one thing that makes a house an easy target, such as a magazine article printing a plan of all the rooms so that a thief knows where everything is kept.
Organisation: a clear title, short self-contained points arranged in a sensible order, and the blanks placed after the body of the notice.
Accuracy and expression: correct grammar and punctuation, notice-style language suited to a school board, kept to about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
NOTICE
Keeping Your Home Safe

Our school is running a safety drive on protecting the home. Please follow these precautions:

• Keep your jewellery and money in a bank, not in a safe at home.
• Never hang the key to your house or kitchen door on a hook outside.
• Have a strong burglar alarm fitted, and get it checked often.

One habit that makes a house an easy target is letting a magazine article print a plan of all the rooms, so that a thief already knows where everything is kept.

Take care!

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your literature teacher asks you to explain, step by step, how the young lady who came to the house at Shotover Grange managed to trick Horace Danby into opening her own safe for her. Write your answer in about 120 words, giving the steps in order.

markingPoints.description: She interrupts him from the doorway by asking whether it is a cold or hay fever, so he answers without thinking and is taken off guard.
She seems amused at meeting a burglar, which gives Horace the hope that he can avoid trouble if he treats her the right way.
She threatens to telephone the police; because he hates the thought of prison, Horace begs to be let go and promises never to do it again.
She picks up a silver box and takes a cigarette from it, so Horace takes off his gloves and gives her his cigarette lighter, which is how his prints are left behind.

She claims she is the lady of the house and has forgotten the numbers to open the safe; he agrees to break it, and she says her husband will not be there for a month and the safe will be mended by then.
The trick fails because his fingerprints are all over the room, nobody believes that the owner’s wife asked him to open the safe, and she calls the story nonsense, so he is arrested.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. She asks from the doorway whether it is a cold or hay fever, so Horace answers without thinking.
2. She seems amused at meeting a burglar, so Horace hopes to avoid trouble if he treats her right.
3. She threatens to telephone the police; hating prison, he begs to be let go and promises to stop.
4. She takes a cigarette from a silver box, so he takes off his gloves and hands her his lighter: his first slip.
5. She says she is the lady of the house and has forgotten the numbers to open her own safe; he agrees to break it, and her husband is away for a month.
6. His prints are all over the room, nobody believes the owner’s wife sent him, and he is arrested.
